extracted.intended_audience: general readers and students of history/philosophy
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative principles for writing and presenting history and intellectual/philosophical ideas to a general audience, emphasizing openness, accessibility, and avoiding pedantry or corruptions of doctrine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Openness and directness of intellectual life
rubrics_metrics.description: Right thinking is necessarily an open process; the vital air of true intellectual life is freedom, openness, and directness of statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserve centres of philosophy and research from the 'caking and darkening accumulations of narrow and dingy-spirited specialists.' Ensure ideas are expressed plainly and directly rather than locked away in inaccessible scholarship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility and plain availability of knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: The only science and history of full value to men consist of what is generally and clearly known.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep all that can be thought and known plainly, honestly, and easily available to ordinary men and women; avoid concentrating results in a hidden 'dark lantern' (Museum/Library) accessible only by costly travel or tedious letter-writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration of learning with practical affairs
rubrics_metrics.description: A man of learning should be none the less a man of affairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scholarship should not withdraw wholly from ordinary life; intellectuals should participate in public life and practical affairs so that knowledge benefits society rather than becoming a secluded priesthood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of pedantry and specialist obscurantism
rubrics_metrics.description: Warning against the rise of the ‘Scholarly Man’: shy, eccentric, unpractical, incapable of essentials, fierce upon trivialities, jealous of colleagues, intolerant, obscurantist and preferring inaccessible rare books.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not substitute the use of books for worship of books. Avoid methods that make work deliberately tedious or inaccessible (excessive copying difficulty, hoarding rare books). Encourage scholarship that is practical, generous, and communicative rather than petty, jealous, and secretive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of enumeration and mnemonic devices in oral cultures
rubrics_metrics.description: In undocumented/oral societies, enumerations (e.g., Eightfold Path, Four Truths) are a mnemonic necessity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When producing teaching for audiences without written texts, structure doctrines in numbered, pithy aphorisms and lists to aid memorization and transmission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eightfold Path as criteria for right conduct and teaching
rubrics_metrics.description: The Aryan Path (Eightfold Path) enumerates elements for escape from selfish craving: Right Views, Right Aspirations, Right Speech, Right Conduct, Right Livelihood, Right Effort, Right Mindfulness, Right Rapture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these elements as practical standards for evaluating ethical/religious life: insist on truth (Right Views), encourage altruistic aspirations (Right Aspirations), ensure ethical speech and behaviour (Right Speech/Conduct), promote an honest livelihood, disciplined effort, constant mindfulness against personal glory, and guardedness against pointless ecstasy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Religion judged by conduct rather than ritual or theology
rubrics_metrics.description: Primitive Buddhism is primarily a religion of conduct, not a religion of observances and sacrifices; it had no temples, priests, or systematic theology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate religions or moral systems by their effects on conduct and ethical life rather than the richness of ritual, sacrificial forms, or theological speculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid propagation through fabricated marvels and dishonest propaganda
rubrics_metrics.description: Criticism that disciples often invent miracles and marvels about a teacher ('honest but stupid disciples will tell lies for the glory of their master') to impress the outer world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Propagation of ideas should avoid fabrication and sensationalism; truthful, reasoned presentation is preferable to constructing marvels or falsehoods to attract followers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection of extreme asceticism in favour of balanced means
rubrics_metrics.description: Gautama rejected extreme self-torture and asceticism as a means to wisdom, concluding that 'whatever truth a man may reach is reached best by a nourished brain in a healthy body.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Endorse a middle way: avoid extremes that sacrifice practical health or engagement; encourage disciplined effort and proper bodily care to support intellectual and spiritual pursuits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim of emancipation from selfish craving as measure of religious success
rubrics_metrics.description: The fundamental teaching: suffering arises from insatiable selfishness/craving (sensuousness, desire for personal immortality, desire for prosperity); emancipation (Nirvana) is the extinction of futile personal aims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess religious/philosophical systems by whether they diagnose the causes of suffering realistically and provide practical means to transform or extinguish selfish cravings, rather than promising merely ritual or magical remedies.
